content: 1. Barriers to accessing antiretroviral therapy in developing countries have been extensively reviewed, highlighting the challenges faced by populations in resource-limited settings. (Trop Med Int Health, 2008) 2. Food insecurity has been identified as a significant barrier to maintaining adherence to antiretroviral therapy in Uganda, as demonstrated in a study exploring its impact on treatment outcomes. (PLoS One, 2010) 3. Thematic analysis, as a reflexive approach, has been utilized to explore qualitative data in health research, providing insights into complex issues. (Accessed June 2021) 4. Factors influencing the uptake of HIV care and treatment among children in South Africa were examined through a qualitative study involving caregivers and clinic staff, revealing critical barriers and facilitators. (AIDS Care, 2010) 5. Missed opportunities for initiating antiretroviral therapy in HIV-infected children under two years of age in West Africa were documented, emphasizing the need for timely interventions. (J Int AIDS Soc, 2016) 6. A qualitative study in sub-Saharan Africa identified barriers and facilitators to pediatric antiretroviral therapy adherence, offering valuable insights for improving treatment outcomes. (AIDS Patient Care STDs, 2011) 7. Self-reported and caregiver-reported barriers to medication adherence in HIV-infected children and youth were analyzed, shedding light on the multifaceted challenges they face. (Pediatrics, 2012) 8. Caregivers of virally non-suppressed children in Uganda's intensive adherence counseling program reported numerous challenges, as revealed in a qualitative study. (BMC Health Serv Res, 2019) 9. Pediatric adherence to HIV antiretroviral therapy remains a critical issue, with studies emphasizing the importance of tailored interventions to address unique challenges in this population. (Curr HIV/AIDS Rep, 2009) 10. Increasing access to antiretroviral drugs for children with HIV infection has been a priority, with recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics highlighting strategies to improve treatment coverage. (Pediatrics, 2007) 11. The response to antiretroviral therapy following a single peripartum dose of nevirapine was evaluated, providing insights into treatment efficacy and resistance patterns. (N Engl J Med, 2007) 12. A systematic review examined HIV-1 resistance-associated mutations in children experiencing first-line antiretroviral treatment failure in resource-poor regions, underscoring the need for robust treatment strategies. (Lancet Infect Dis, 2011) 13. UNICEF's 2009 country fact sheets on children and AIDS provided critical data on the state of pediatric HIV care and treatment globally. (UNICEF, 2009) 14. Children growing up with HIV face unique challenges, and their success in managing the disease depends on comprehensive support systems, as highlighted in a Lancet article. (Lancet, 2014) 15. A systematic review of global qualitative evidence identified barriers and facilitators to improving antiretroviral therapy adherence, offering actionable recommendations for intervention design. (J Int AIDS Soc, 2016) 16. The linkage, initiation, and retention of children in the antiretroviral therapy cascade were reviewed, providing an overview of strategies to enhance pediatric HIV care. (AIDS, 2013) 17. A framework for improving HIV service delivery for infants, children, and adolescents was developed to guide country-level programming efforts. (UNICEF, 2020) 18. A screening tool to identify older children living with HIV in high-prevalence settings was validated, demonstrating its utility in primary care facilities. (AIDS, 2016) 19. A simple screening tool was developed to identify high-risk children for targeted HIV testing in Malawian inpatient wards, improving diagnostic efficiency. (J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr, 2018) 20. A randomized trial in Uganda compared home-based and clinic-based HIV testing among household members of individuals on antiretroviral therapy, revealing differences in acceptability and outcomes. (J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr, 2010) 21. Pediatric HIV testing beyond the context of prevention of mother-to-child transmission was systematically reviewed, emphasizing the need for expanded diagnostic approaches. (Lancet HIV, 2016) 22. Routine HIV testing for hospitalized pediatric patients in Zambia was found to be both acceptable and feasible, as demonstrated in a study conducted at a university teaching hospital. (J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr, 2009) 23. A systematic review evaluated the performance and clinical utility of point-of-care HIV-1 RNA testing for diagnosis and care, highlighting its potential in resource-limited settings. (PLoS One, 2019) 24. Differentiated service delivery models for pediatric HIV care and treatment were implemented in sub-Saharan Africa, with studies documenting their opportunities, challenges, and outcomes. (Fam Med Community Health, 2020) 25. Scaling up access to antiretroviral therapy for children in rural Zambia was evaluated through a cohort study, demonstrating the effectiveness of mobile and hospital-affiliated HIV clinics. (PLoS One, 2014) 26. Family ART adherence clubs in South Africa were shown to promote pediatric ART adherence and retention, with positive outcomes for children receiving treatment. (Accessed June 2021) 27. Community-based mentor mothers were found to be an acceptable support mechanism for HIV-positive pregnant women on antiretroviral therapy in Kenya, as revealed in a qualitative study. (BMC Pregnancy Childbirth, 2019) 28. The Mentor Mother Program in Uganda demonstrated a positive effect on the retention of mother-baby pairs in HIV care, based on secondary analysis of program data. (PLoS One, 2019) 29. Disclosure of HIV status to children in resource-limited settings was systematically reviewed, identifying predictors and challenges associated with this process. (J Int AIDS Soc, 2013) 30. Caregivers' lack of disclosure skills was found to delay the disclosure of perinatal HIV status to children in resource-limited communities, as shown in a multicenter qualitative study. (Nurs Res Pract, 2016) 31. A study in Papua New Guinea explored HIV status disclosure and education for children and adolescents, emphasizing the importance of tailored communication strategies. (J Paediatr Child Health, 2018) 32. Adolescent-friendly health services for adolescents living with HIV were developed, transitioning from theoretical frameworks to practical implementation. (Accessed June 2021) 33. Recent interventions to improve retention in HIV care and adherence to antiretroviral therapy among adolescents and youth were systematically reviewed, providing evidence-based recommendations. (AIDS Patient Care STDs, 2019) 34. A practical guide was developed to meaningfully engage adolescents in the AIDS response, emphasizing their role in ending the epidemic. (Accessed June 2021) 35. Differentiated service delivery models for adolescents with HIV in Zimbabwe were evaluated, demonstrating their impact on virological failure rates. (Lancet Glob Health, 2020) 36. Operation Triple Zero in Kenya empowered adolescents and young people living with HIV to take control of their health, with promising outcomes. (PEPFAR, 2018) 37. Psychosocial support for HIV-positive adolescents in Zimbabwe was enhanced through targeted interventions, improving their overall well-being. (PLoS One, 2013) 38. National quality standards for adolescent-friendly health services were developed to ensure the delivery of appropriate care for this population. (WHO, 2012) 39. A quality improvement intervention for adolescent depression in primary care clinics was found to be effective, as demonstrated in a randomized controlled trial. (JAMA, 2005) 40. Motivational interventions were shown to reduce rapid subsequent births among adolescent mothers, as evidenced by a community-based randomized trial. (Ann Fam Med, 2009) 41. Cell phone support for non-adherent HIV-infected youth and young adults was evaluated in an initial randomized controlled trial, showing potential for improving adherence. (AIDS Behav, 2014) 42. A study evaluated the provision of additional midwifery support to teenage mothers, highlighting its impact on maternal and child health outcomes. (Public Health, 2011) 43. A brief motivational intervention for adolescent smokers in medical settings was found to be effective in promoting smoking cessation. (Addict Behav, 2005) 44. The Regai Dzive Shiri Project in Zimbabwe demonstrated the effectiveness of a randomized intervention in improving adolescent sexual and reproductive health outcomes.
